title: Hail! Father, Son, and Spirit Great
description: Hail! Father, Son, and Spirit Great in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 256.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail! Fa-ther, Son, and Spir-it great, Be-fore the birth of time En-throned in ev-er-last-ing state, JE-HO-VAH, E-LO-HIM!

lines: Hail! Father, Son, and Spirit great,
From thee our being we receive,
And, raised out of the earth, we live
Thy powerful, wise, and loving mind
And all the glorious Persons joined
Again thou did'st, in council met,
And when we rise in love renewed,
An image of the Triune God,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
